questions.q: The main downside of the coaxial X8 layout?
questions.explain: The lower prop works in the upper prop's wash. You pay for compactness and fault tolerance with efficiency.

questions.q: What do you fix first with high VIBE on big props?
options: The PID gains and D-term filters on the yaw axis
questions.explain: Balancing props and motors, frame stiffness, FC damping. Filters are the last resort.

questions.q: When do you test a motor failure?
options: SITL, then at altitude without a payload
Right away with the full payload, to test the worst case
On the bench with props on
questions.explain: Fault tolerance is tested, not assumed.
Hover throttle, refined in flight; altitude hold depends on it.

options: The maximum bank angle in centidegrees
The output headroom reserved for yaw
questions.explain: The motor output headroom (PWM) reserved for yaw at saturation; yaw is the mixer's lowest priority.

questions.q: How do you safely test a motor failure on an X8?
options: Remove a prop right in flight
An applet in SITL, then without a payload
Disconnect an ESC on the ground with props on
There is no way to test it
questions.explain: motor_failure_test first in SITL, then at altitude without a payload; MOT_STOP_BITMASK + a switch.

questions.q: Why is a heavy vehicle tuned slower and more carefully than a 5"?
options: Large inertia and slow motors: errors build up longer and are more dangerous
ArduPilot does not support big props
questions.explain: Big props and mass mean slow dynamics and a high cost of error.
